Classgrid includes several notification paths: web notification routes, email delivery for authentication and onboarding, push registration routes, Android Firebase handling, platform announcements, changelog, support replies, and module-specific notifications. Actual delivery depends on provider credentials and deployment configuration.
Prerequisites
Logged-in user for web notifications and push registration
Email provider configuration for OTP and transactional email
Firebase/FCM configuration for native push
Correct user roles for broadcast or admin notification routes
Step 1 - Use email for account security

The auth system sends emails for device OTP, password reset, activation, and onboarding verification. Students also receive onboarding OTP through the student API. If emails are delayed, check provider settings, resend timers, and rate limits before retrying repeatedly.
Step 2 - Register devices for push

The push API includes device registration and unregistration routes. The Android wrapper includes Firebase messaging handling and opens deep links for notification types such as assignment, grade, live class, chat, fee, canteen, exam, and announcement.
Step 3 - Send role-based notifications

Push routes support sending messages to individual targets, by role, or broadcast from authorized roles. Organization admins have broader broadcast access than faculty. The web app also includes notification pages in student and faculty navigation.
Step 4 - Use platform announcements

Super admin navigation includes Notifications Engine, Announcements, Changelog, Helpdesk Chat, Support Tickets, Feedback, and Reviews. These surfaces support platform communication and operational follow-up.
Delivery Notes

Treat notification delivery as a chain. The message must be created by the correct route, the recipient must have the right role or device registration, and the provider must be configured. For mobile push, the Android wrapper handles Firebase messages and opens role-aware deep links. For email, the backend uses configured mail services for OTP, reset, activation, and other transactional messages. For in-app notifications, verify that the user can access the linked route before sending broad announcements.
Common Mistakes
Assuming push notifications work before Firebase credentials are configured
Retrying OTP sends until rate-limited
Sending broadcasts from a role that is not permitted
Forgetting that Android deep links depend on matching app routes
Sending a notification to a module the recipient role cannot open

Classgrid reporting is module-based. The codebase includes analytics dashboards, export endpoints, and operational summaries across admissions, fees, attendance, examinations, library, organization administration, and super admin operations. There is no single universal report builder in the scanned code, so reports should be generated from the relevant module.
Prerequisites
Correct role for the report area
Live records in the selected module
Date range, hierarchy, classroom, division, or status filters where applicable
Export permissions for compliance or backup routes
Step 1 - Use admission reports

Admission dashboards include funnel metrics, daily and cumulative trends, category distribution, seat type breakdown, document status, fee collection, merit round histograms, branch fill rates, RLA details, recent applications, SMS budget, live seat matrix, and active configuration. Export routes exist for DTE, SARAL, AICTE, and State Board formats.
Step 2 - Use fee reports

The fees dashboard exposes collection totals, payable amounts, pending and overdue values, paid/partial/unpaid counts, collection rate, payment mode breakdown, daily trends, recent transactions, and defaulters. Older fee-record routes also expose summaries and reminders.

Looking for all reports in one global screen
Running exports from a role without permission
Expecting dashboard numbers before source records exist
Using scaffolded dashboard cards as compliance-ready reports without verifying API data

Classgrid user management combines platform-level organization provisioning, organization admin activation, role-based dashboard access, student onboarding, faculty activation, trusted-device verification, and department role assignment. Access problems are usually caused by wrong role, missing organization, inactive status, or incomplete activation.
Prerequisites
Super admin access for platform-wide organization and user operations
Organization admin access for institution-level users
Correct email addresses for invitations, OTP, and password reset
Role plan for the institution
Step 1 - Confirm organization ownership

Every institution user should belong to the correct organization. The backend blocks non-super-admin users when tenant context does not match their organization. Organization status also matters: suspended, blocked, inactive, maintenance, or globally locked states can block login.
Step 2 - Activate admin and faculty accounts

New organization admins use activation token or activation code flows. Faculty activation and forced password reset flows are separate from normal password reset. Use the correct activation path to avoid expired-token confusion.
Step 3 - Assign the correct role

Assign the narrowest role that matches the user's work. Students and faculty receive workspace launchers. Department users should receive roles such as admissions, fees, exams, library, attendance, HR, or hostel when those dashboards are needed. Super admin should remain limited to platform operators.
Step 4 - Complete student onboarding

Students may need onboarding OTP verification, division selection, PRN or roll number validation, academic history, address, and profile completion. The API validates organization and division context.
Step 5 - Troubleshoot access

Check the login portal, role, organization assignment, user status, email verification, device OTP, and organization status. For missing navigation, inspect role first. For invalid student onboarding, inspect division, PRN, and roll number uniqueness.
Common Mistakes
Giving super admin access to institution staff
Using password reset instead of activation for new admins
Assigning faculty without an organization
Creating duplicate PRNs or roll numbers
